Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. input.prompt:
In this repository, find the code path where the server delivers outbound HTTP notifications to external systems when content changes (e.g., webhooks). I need:

1. The specific function that actually performs the outbound HTTP request (executes the delivery) — file path and function/method name.
2. Any mechanism that protects this from SSRF (server-side request forgery) — i.e., prevents the webhook URL from pointing at internal/private network addresses (like 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.x, 192.168.x, etc.) — file path and function/mechanism name.

Search for terms like "webhook", "notify", "dispatch", "deliver", SSRF, "isPrivate", "isInternal", "blocklist", "allowlist", IP validation, DNS rebinding protection, etc.

Report back with exact file paths (relative to repo root) and function names for both the delivery execution and the SSRF protection. Be thorough — check for a shared HTTP client/fetch wrapper that might apply the protection centrally rather than at the call site.

content.text:
h02.
delivery function — `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (invoked synchronously, or asynchronously via `PostAsync`/`asyncPostQueue` in the same file), which issues the outbound HTTP POST via the package-level `safeClient`.

protection mechanism — `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59` (the `http.Transport.DialContext` used by `safeClient`), which resolves the target host and rejects any address in a reserved/private range via `isReservedIP` in `internal/webhook/validate.go:44`. The same `isReservedIP`/`reservedNetworks` check (covering loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/cloud IMDS `169.254.169.254`, and IPv6 equivalents) is also applied at webhook-creation time by `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go:62`, so both dial-time and configuration-time checks guard against SSRF (dial-time also defeats DNS-rebinding, since resolution happens right before connecting).
